{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Support and Interface Licence)

**To:** Deal team, Mortgage Logic.com (Client)  
**From:** In-house counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — issues, walk-away items and next steps

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified **six positions we must fix** (two critical, two high, two medium) and **three items requiring internal confirmation**. The commercial protections we would normally expect from a vendor hosting our web site, Client Content and borrower credit data are largely absent, while the obligations running against us are broad.

The two critical issues are the risk-allocation provisions in Section 12. TrueLink's indemnity is limited to breach of the Agreement, with **no third-party IP infringement indemnity anywhere in the document** and no non-infringement warranty for a breach-based indemnity to bite on; at the same time we give a very broad indemnity covering our breach, Client Content, the Web Site and product/service injury. That imbalance is compounded by a **one-sided liability cap**: TrueLink alone is capped at 12 months' hosting and support compensation (and only as to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11), while our liability, including under the broad indemnity, is entirely uncapped. There is also no mutual exclusion of indirect or consequential damages. Uncapped Customer liability against a capped Vendor is a walk-away item under the playbook.

Three further gaps follow from the same drafting approach: **no ownership provision in our favour** (TrueLink's rights in the Interface are confirmed, but nothing confirms our ownership of Client Content, Client IP, our borrower/loan data, or the Support Services work product we pay for); **no vendor insurance obligation at all** (a walk-away trigger for a vendor processing personal data); **no post-termination transition assistance or data return**, with Section 13 instead putting the migration burden on us (30 days for a new name server, 60 days for new hosting); and **no meaningful performance warranty** (TrueLink's only express warranty is Y2K date processing, with no conformance or workmanlike-services standard and no repair/replace/refund remedy). The licence grant runs to "Client" alone, excluding our affiliates and contractors, and Section 15 requires TrueLink's absolute consent to assignment with no successor/M&A carve-out — which would let TrueLink block a corporate transaction.

The Agreement is, however, favourable to us in several important respects and we are not proposing redlines there: no exclusivity or non-compete on us (Section 2(a) expressly preserves our right to acquire, develop or licence competing software and services), no liquidated damages or termination charge, no MFN or audit right running against us (Section 6 gives us a most-favoured-rate commitment from TrueLink), a 12-month term with 30-day mutual non-renewal and a unilateral at-will exit for us, and California law and courts (the playbook fallback). The Section 5(a) monthly minimum sits at the fallback and is not redlined.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Vendor indemnity limited to breach of contract; no third-party IP infringement indemnity, against a very broad Client indemnity in 12(a). Fails the fallback. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Cap protects TrueLink only (12 months' compensation, Sections 3/4/7/11); Client liability uncapped. No mutual consequential-damages exclusion. Walk-away territory. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Section 15 requires absolute consent; no successor/M&A carve-out and no change-of-control language anywhere. Approaches walk-away. |
| High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | Only § 2(d) (TrueLink's Interface rights). No Client ownership of Client Content, Client IP, data or § 4 work product; fails the fallback. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | § 2(a) grant runs to "Client" only; affiliates and contractors unlicensed and no mechanism to add them; not transferable to a successor. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | Non-exclusive licence; § 2(a) expressly preserves competing procurement. § 3(i) credit-report requirement noted as channel-tied only. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No LDs, penalties or early-termination charge. Blank monthly minimums noted as a pricing point. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us; the separate Non-Competition Agreement limits TrueLink's Credit Data use. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Needs review | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Assessed compliant at preferred position (Section 14 at-will exit, ~30–60 days, no exit fee), but verification failed and Section 4 is not in the reviewed text. See Next steps. |
| Medium | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No insurance obligation in the document. Walk-away trigger for a vendor processing personal data. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No migration assistance and no return-or-destroy mechanic; Section 13 places the migration burden on us. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Only a Y2K warranty (Section 9); no conformance, services, compliance or malicious-code warranty and no remedy. Fails the fallback. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review | § 5 COMPENSATION. | Assessed compliant: no audit right runs against us, and § 6 / § 3(e) verification rights run in our favour. Verification failed as a heuristic artefact. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Assessed compliant: no non-solicit or no-hire covenant on us. Verification failed as a heuristic artefact. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | California law (§ 26) and exclusive California venue (§ 27) — at the fallback. No arbitration. Local-county venue noted only. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No MFN on us; § 6 gives us a most-favoured-rate commitment from TrueLink. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments on Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | § 5(a) minimum sits at the fallback: 12-month term, unilateral at-will exit, no shortfall penalty or acceleration. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | One-year renewals with mutual 30-day opt-out (§ 13) — preferred position. No renewal reminder or uplift cap; noted only. |

## Walk-away items

1. **Uncapped Client liability against a capped Vendor (§ 12).** The cap protects TrueLink alone while our liability, including under the broad 12(a) indemnity, is unlimited. We require a mutual cap of general application at the greater of 12 months' compensation and USD 1,000,000, with Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) outside it, and confirmation that our payment obligations sit outside the limitation.
2. **No vendor insurance.** TrueLink hosts our Web Site, Client Content and customer credit data with no coverage obligation. We require the inserted Section 31 (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O including tech E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request); fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.
3. **Assignment consent with no M&A carve-out (§ 15).** As drafted, TrueLink could block a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of our assets. We require the affiliate/successor carve-out on written notice, a reasonableness standard on consent, no assignment by TrueLink to a Client competitor, and confirmation that a change of control of Client is not an assignment and triggers no termination or re-pricing right.

We would also treat the absence of any IP infringement indemnity as a red line in practice, given there is no non-infringement warranty behind it.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the six items requiring change: vendor indemnity (add IP infringement, breach of law, unauthorised access to Client Content, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, plus notice/control/cooperation procedure); mutual liability cap with carve-outs; assignment and change of control; Client ownership of Client Content, Client IP, Client data and Support Services work product (assignment from TrueLink with a licence back for embedded TrueLink IP, no joint ownership); licence extension to our affiliates and contractors with mutual successor-transfer rights; and the Section 9 performance/conformance warranty with a repair-replace-refund remedy.
2. **Insert the missing clauses**: new Section 31 (insurance) and transition assistance and data return/deletion in Section 14 (six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable export within 30 days, then deletion with written certification subject to legally required retention).
3. **Obtain and review Section 4**, which is not in the reviewed text. Section 14 opens "Subject to Section 4 hereof," and Section 6 indicates Section 4 concerns minimum monthly fees. If Section 4 preserves minimum monthly fees after termination or otherwise conditions our exit, it may operate as a de facto exit charge and we will reopen the termination-for-convenience analysis.
4. **Clear the three needs-review items internally.** T4C, AUDIT and NOSOLICIT were each assessed as compliant on the reviewed text; the failed checks reflect drafting phrasing (an obliquely drafted convenience right) or the absence of any clause to measure, not identified risk. We will record the basis on file. Subject to item 3 above, no redline is proposed.
5. **Commercial items for the business team**: complete the blank minimum monthly amounts in § 5(a)/§ 6 with figures reflecting realistic baseline usage before signature, and note that § 6 carves the minimums out of our documentation and charge-contest rights. If renewal economics are negotiated, we will raise a 60-day renewal reminder and a CPI/3% uplift cap as goodwill asks (post-year-one uplifts are currently uncapped).
6. **Request the separate Non-Competition Agreement** for independent review; it is referenced in § 8(d) but is not before us.
7. **Administrative**: conform the survival cross-reference ("Sections 1 and 5 through 30") to the new Section 31.
"}
